finding.claim: TagReference.create passes the caller's tag name to `git tag` without a `--` separator or leading-dash validation, so a name such as `-f` or `-d` is parsed as a git option. This bypasses the `force=False` default and can overwrite or delete existing tags.
finding.source: `path` parameter of TagReference.create (git/refs/tag.py:91-95), caller-controlled tag name
finding.sink: repo.git.tag(*args) at git/refs/tag.py:160, where args=(path, reference) at tag.py:158

trace.note: path and reference arrive as caller-supplied strings
unsafe_git_tag_options is only ["--file", "-F"]; -f and -d are not blocked
-f is added to kwargs only when force=True, so an injected -f bypasses the force flag
repo.git.tag(*args, **kwargs) executes git tag with the injected flag
returns TagReference for refs/tags/<path>, which does not match the actual effect

finding.claim: Git.ls_remote checks only blocked options (--upload-pack, --exec) and never runs the URL through check_unsafe_protocols, so an ext:: remote-helper URL is passed to git ls-remote unchecked. Exploitation requires git to allow the ext protocol, which I believe is disabled by default in modern git but did not verify.
finding.source: URL positional argument to Git.ls_remote (git/cmd.py:1130), caller-controlled
finding.sink: _call_process("ls_remote", *args) at git/cmd.py:1144, which runs git ls-remote with the URL

trace.note: ls_remote accepts *args, including the remote URL

check_unsafe_protocols exists (regex (.+)::.+ at cmd.py:650) but is not called on this path; it is called on clone, remote create, set_url, fetch, pull, push and archive paths
